intro: The verb ir, the words al and del, and the ways of getting around the city.
b1.texto:
The verb **ir** (to go) is irregular. It is conjugated like this:

- yo **voy** (I go)
- tú **vas** (you go)
- él / ella / usted **va** (he / she / you formal go)
- nosotros **vamos** (we go)
- vosotros **vais** (you all go)
- ellos **van** (they go)

To say where you are going, use **a**:

- Voy **a** la playa. (I go to the beach.)
- Voy **al** centro. (I go to the centre.)

Notice: **a + el = al**. And in the plural, **a + los = a los**.
b4.titulo: Al, del and how to get around
b4.texto:
Two contractions you need to master:

- **a + el = al**: «Voy **al** centro».
- **de + el = del**: «Vengo **del** trabajo».

You never say «a el» or «de el».

And for getting around:

- **en metro** (by metro), **en autobús** (by bus), **en tren** (by train), **en coche** (by car), **en bici** (by bike)
- **a pie** (on foot), when you are walking
b5.f0.texto: Lucía and Pablo go to the centre on Saturday.
b5.f1.texto: They go by metro because the bus is slow.
b5.f2.texto: The centre is near the beach.
b5.f3.texto: There are lots of shops and cafés there.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía wants to buy a present.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo is looking for a book in the bookshop.
b5.f6.texto: They have a coffee with milk afterwards.
b5.f7.texto: They go back home at half past six.
b6.pregunta: How do Lucía and Pablo get to the centre?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the text says they go by metro.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The bus is slow, so they do not take it.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Lucía goes on foot on other days, but that Saturday they go by metro.
b7.pregunta: Complete with the correct form of «ir».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «va» goes with él (he), ella (she) or usted (formal you).
b8.traduccion: I go to the centre by metro.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I go to the centre on foot».
p.voy.consejo: It is written with «v» but sounds like «b»: «voy».
p.vas.consejo: It is written with «v» but sounds like «bas».
p.va.consejo: It is very short: just one syllable, and it sounds like «ba».
p.vamos.consejo: It also works to suggest something: «¡Vamos!» means let's go.
p.van.consejo: The verb «ir» for «ellos» or «ustedes»: it is written with «v» and sounds «ban».
p.adónde.consejo: It has an accent because it asks a question, and it is written as one word: «adónde».
p.al.consejo: You never write «a el»: it is always «al».
p.del.consejo: You never write «de el»: it is always «del».
p.el centro.consejo: The «c» before «e» sounds «th» in Spain: THEN-tro.
p.la playa.consejo: You say both «en la playa» (being there) and «a la playa» (going there).
p.en metro.consejo: To say how you travel, use «en»: «en metro», «en tren», «en coche».
p.a pie.consejo: Always with the preposition «a»: «a pie». «En pie» means standing up.
p.lento.consejo: The opposite of «rápido». The feminine is «lenta»: «un tren lento», «una clase lenta».
p.cafeterías.consejo: The accent on «í» breaks the pair «ia» into two syllables: ka-fe-te-RI-as. The singular is «cafetería».
p.toman.consejo: «Tomar» means to take, but with food or drink it means to have: «toman un café con leche».
p.vuelven.consejo: From «volver»: the stem «o» becomes «ue» in «vuelven». «Volver a casa» means to go back home.
